title: Layered Alginate Constructs: A Platform for Co-culture of Heterogeneous Cell Populations
protocol: Prepare a 4% (w/v) alginate solution in 1x Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline without added calcium chloride or magnesium chloride.
Place the alginate solution in a 37 °C water bath.
Mix the alginate solution at a ratio of 1:1 with warm cell culture media base, resulting in a 2% (w/v) alginate concentration.
Sterilize the alginate/media solution using sterile 0.2 µm nylon syringe filters.
Prepare a bath of sterile 102 mM calcium chloride dihydrate in sterile water.
Cut thick filter paper to the size of the bottom endplate and place it in the calcium chloride bath until saturated, approximately 1 min.
Cut a cell microsieve membrane (10 µm pore size) to the size of the bottom endplate and place it in the calcium chloride bath until saturated, approximately 1 min.
Set up one half (the bottom half) of the mold construct.
Place a large endplate (3 in x 3 in) atop a thick filter paper.
Place a microsieve membrane on top of the filter paper.
Smooth the stack using a sterile spatula.
Invert and press the stack onto a stack of paper towels to remove excess calcium chloride solution.
Place the gel formation mold with cylindrical wells on top of the microsieve membrane.
Gently fasten the mold together on two sides using binder clips, leaving room for the top endplate (1.5 in x 3 in).
Place a small endplate atop a thick filter paper.
Place a microsieve membrane on top of the filter paper.
Smooth the stack using a sterile spatula.
Invert and press this half of the mold onto a stack of paper towels to remove excess calcium chloride solution.
Do not fasten this half of the mold with binder clips at this time.
Culture cells according to manufacturer's instructions.
Harvest desired cells for embedding in layered alginate hydrogels.
Use a cell density of 1 - 2 x 10^6 cells/ml, as recommended.
Seed mesenchymal stem cells at a density of 3,000 - 5,000 cells/cm² in T-75 flasks containing basal growth media.
Remove spent media every 2 - 3 days and replace with fresh basal growth media until cells reach 80 - 90% confluency.
Rinse mesenchymal stem cells with 3 ml of 1x Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline (without calcium chloride or magnesium chloride).
Add 3 ml of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to the T-75 flasks and incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
After cells have detached, add 6 - 9 ml of basal growth media to neutralize trypsin-EDTA.
Centrifuge mesenchymal stem cells at 600 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant and re-suspend cells in 1 - 5 ml of basal growth media.
Count cells using a hemocytometer according to device instructions.
Remove 1 x 10^6 cells from total cell suspension, centrifuge under same conditions as before, and aspirate the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cell pellet with 1 ml of sterile alginate/media solution to achieve a cell density of 1 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Pipette 130 μl of the cell-alginate mixture into six 6 mm diameter x 3 mm tall wells in the bottom half of the mold construct dropwise, avoiding bubbles.
Smooth the top half of the mold construct using a sterile spatula and place it over the wells containing the cell-alginate mixture.
Cover the wells completely with the top half of the mold construct.
Fasten the top and bottom halves of the mold construct using binder clips while pressing down firmly on the center.
Immerse the fastened mold construct in a 102 mM calcium chloride bath, ensuring full submersion.
Incubate the mold construct in the cell culture hood at room temperature for 90 min.
Remove the mold construct from the 102 mM calcium chloride bath.
Place the mold construct on a stack of paper towels in the cell culture hood.
Remove all four binder clips to separate the two halves of the mold construct.
Trace the edge of the wells containing hydrogels with a spatula to loosen them carefully.
Wedge out the hydrogels from the wells.
Drop the hydrogels directly into a bath of 1x Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline with calcium chloride and magnesium chloride.
Cover the gels completely in the buffer solution for washing, for 1 - 5 min.
Transfer the hydrogels into basal growth media solution that covers them completely.
Incubate the hydrogels in a cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for at least 1 hr.
Fasten a mold with 6 mm diameter x 1.5 mm tall wells to an endplate using binder clips on both sides to create the "cutting mold".
Fasten a mold with 9 mm diameter x 3 mm tall wells to an endplate using binder clips on both sides to create the "annealing mold".
Prepare a solution of 100 mM sodium citrate/30 mM EDTA in sterile water.
Remove gels containing hMSCs from media in the dish.
Place each gel into the "cutting mold" wells, ensuring they fit snugly with half protruding above the mold.
Using a scalpel, slice the gel along the surface of the mold.
Flip the top half of the gel and place it into an open mold well.
Repeat with second gel.
Place a piece of dry cell microsieve membrane on top of the wells.
Pipette a solution of 100 mM sodium citrate/30 mM EDTA onto the thick filter paper until saturated.
Incubate the gels for 1 min at room temperature.
Remove the cell microsieve membrane and thick filter paper.
Remove the binder clips and open the mold.
Transfer one sodium citrate/EDTA-treated half of the hydrogel to the prepared "annealing mold" with the cut surface facing upwards.

Lift and place a second sodium citrate/EDTA-treated half-gel onto the gel already in the "annealing mold", flipping this second half-gel so that the cut surface is in contact with the first gel's cut surface.
Press gently down on the two gels using a spatula to remove any bubbles between them.
Submerge the "annealing mold" containing the gels in a 102 mM calcium chloride bath for 30 min without covering it with an endplate.
Remove the "annealing mold" from the calcium chloride bath and place it onto paper towels.
Remove the binder clips to separate the mold from the endplate.
Collect the annealed gels using a spatula and place them into a 1x Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline with calcium chloride and magnesium chloride bath for washing.
Transfer the annealed hydrogels to cell culture media in a desired dish (e.g., 6-well plate) for culture.
